basis: Becker nevus with defining ipsilateral muscle and skeletal hypoplasia; breast hypoplasia has no axis.
Permanent congenital laryngeal paralysis and intellectual disability define the syndrome; bronchiectasis also supports pulmonary involvement.
Severe neonatal epileptic encephalopathy; optic disc pallor in 2/2 supports optic nerve damage. Dysphagia and apnea reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Immune-mediated progressive hemispheric encephalitis with seizures and cerebral atrophy; visual loss is occasional and may be central.
Defining intellectual disability, skeletal malformations and abnormal hair; conductive hearing impairment occurs in 80-99%. Nonspecific immune annotation does not establish immune disease.
B-cell lymphoma arising predominantly in the stomach; lymphoid malignancy supports both haematologic and lymphoma mechanism axes.
Hereditary polycystic disease of bone; supplied information supports skeletal disease without established extraskeletal involvement.
Syndromic intellectual disability and microcephaly; hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%. Small testes alone do not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Progressive brainstem and white-matter degeneration; vomiting, abnormal eye movements and auditory evoked potentials do not establish direct gut, eye or ear damage.
Glycosylation disorder; developmental impairment in 4/4, muscle atrophy in 2/4 and contractures in 1/3; visual impairment in 1/3 and strabismus in 1/2 support ocular dysfunction.
Carcinoma originating in gallbladder epithelium; gallbladder belongs to the hepatic axis.
Waldenstrom lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma with monoclonal IgM production; metabolic ancestry does not establish a metabolic disorder.
Isolated male infertility from abnormal sperm flagella and motility; reproductive dysfunction has no axis.
Renal mineralocorticoid resistance causes salt wasting, hyperkalaemia and metabolic acidosis; extra-renal manifestations are subtype-dependent.
Obstruction at the bladder outlet directly impairs urinary flow; bladder and urethra belong to the renal axis.
Short-rib skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia is a major feature of the defining asphyxiating phenotype. Pancreatic fibrosis and cardiac defects lack established >=30% frequency.
Malignancy arising from cutaneous eccrine sweat glands.
RELA-related immune dysregulation with defining chronic oral ulceration in 4/4; ileitis in 1/4. Other immune and cutaneous manifestations are variable.
Disease of the bile ducts, which belong to the hepatic axis; no additional organ applies across this umbrella.
Epidermolytic ichthyosis with skin blistering, scaling and hyperkeratosis; no established extracutaneous disease.
Defined by diabetes, progressive hearing loss and optic atrophy. Broad neurologic and urinary HPO annotations conflict with the subtype-specific definition.
Intrinsic skeletal muscle channelopathy causing myotonia and weakness; dysphagia and episodic stridor do not establish direct gastrointestinal or pulmonary damage.
Familial seizure disorder with intellectual disability and other neurologic features; transient psychotic episodes add no axis.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with progressive spastic paraplegia and cerebral abnormalities; muscle tone changes are neurologic, while skeletal and ocular defects are uncommon.
Broad chromosome 18 anomaly umbrella; neurodevelopmental impairment predominates across pathogenic subtypes. Additional organ defects vary and lack a group-wide frequency.
